memory_update.text: LEU should remain the primary US-listed HALEU/enrichment reference candidate for the nuclear_fuel_and_components node; next layers should test scalability, DOE funding, customer offtake, and deconversion/feedstock constraints.

BWXT is the most defensible public reference name for qualified nuclear components, fuel services, and regulated nuclear manufacturing capacity, but market cap and attention are above the preferred underfollowed range.

MIR is a promising underfollowed second-order candidate in reactor instrumentation, radiation monitoring, dosimetry, and nuclear compliance systems; later layers should quantify Nuclear & Safety exposure to new-build/SMR/fuel-cycle activity.
ASPI belongs only in the speculative_shadow lane until independent uranium/HALEU enrichment validation, regulatory status, definitive offtake/funding, and litigation/disclosure risks are verified.

Additional Layer 1B passes should search niche US-listed nuclear valve, pump, forging, inspection, QA/certification, and EPC suppliers; Curtiss-Wright, Fluor, Graham, and other component-heavy names were not included due to the four-candidate limit.

summary: Expanded the direct US-listed universe for the nuclear fuel-cycle/components/project-execution node. The strongest direct chokepoint exposure is Centrus Energy for US HALEU/enrichment capacity. BWX Technologies remains the reference nuclear-components and fuel-manufacturing leader. The underfollowed lane adds Mirion Technologies as a nuclear instrumentation/radiation-monitoring supplier and ASP Isotopes as a speculative small-cap HALEU/enrichment-technology shadow candidate.
